These developments prompted the construction of the Alaska Highway, a monumental undertaking that aimed to create a military supply route linking the contiguous United States to Alaska through Canada. Constructed in less than a year, the highway addressed concerns about the security of the Alaska Territory and facilitated the transportation of troops, equipment, and supplies to Alaska in anticipation of a potential Japanese invasion.
